title: Augustus, First Emperor
objective: After this level you can explain how Augustus ruled as emperor while claiming to restore the Republic.
summary: In 27 BCE Octavian “restored” the Republic and became Augustus. He kept the old offices but held the legions, and ruled for about 40 years.

cards.headline: He said he was giving power back. He kept almost all of it.
The settlement of 27 BCE
cards.body: In 27 BCE Octavian claimed to restore the Republic, and the Senate gave him the name Augustus, “the revered one.” He called himself princeps, “first citizen,” and avoided the title of king.

cards.headline: Old forms, new power
cards.body: The Senate, consuls and elections continued. But Augustus controlled most of the legions and the key frontier provinces. Historians call his system the Principate, from princeps. He ruled until his death in 14 CE, about 40 years as emperor.
cards.callout: Principate: rule by the princeps, the “first citizen”

cards.fact: Augustus wrote his own record of achievements.
cards.context: Called the Res Gestae, it was inscribed on bronze pillars outside his tomb. It lists his victories, his buildings and his gifts to the Roman people.

cards.headline: The first emperor: crowned without a crown
learned: The old offices survived without real power

options.label: Rex, the old title of king
Dictator for life

questions.explanation: Augustus called himself princeps, “first citizen,” and avoided the title of king.

questions.prompt: Why did Augustus keep the Senate, consuls and elections?

options.label: The Senate and consuls held the real power
The army demanded it
options.rationale: The army was loyal to him.

options.label: To make his rule look like the Republic

questions.explanation: Keeping the old forms let one man’s power look like the Republic, not a monarchy.

questions.prompt: From Level 9: why did Augustus avoid the title of king?
